cues.text: A 35-year-old woman presents with winging of her scapula.
See how the scapula sticks out from her back, like a wing.
This happens because her serratus anterior muscle is paralysed.
The nerve that supplies that muscle has been injured.
It is the long thoracic nerve, also called the long thoracic nerve of Bell.
The long thoracic nerve supplies serratus anterior,
so injury to it paralyses the muscle and causes winging of the scapula.
